title: RE: Larkspur — Thursday workshop
text:
From: Ingrid Halvorsen <i.halvorsen@hallstrom-vane.example.com>
Sent: Wednesday, 9 September 2026 07:52
To: Adaeze Okafor
Cc: Tomasz Wierzbicki
Subject: RE: Larkspur — Thursday workshop

Adaeze,

Agree with Tomasz on all points. Please cancel Thursday, or at least take the plant managers and every commercial item off the agenda. A cultural introduction over lunch is fine; a joint pricing session is not.

I am at DG COMP from 9 to 11 for the state-of-play meeting. Can we speak at 12:30? Tomasz will set up the call.

Ingrid

Sent from my iPhone

-----Original Message-----
From: Tomasz Wierzbicki
Sent: Tuesday, 8 September 2026 22:47
To: Adaeze Okafor
Cc: Ingrid Halvorsen
Subject: RE: Larkspur — Thursday workshop

Dear Adaeze,

Thanks for forwarding Katrin's agenda. Short version: as drafted, the workshop would very likely amount to implementing the concentration before clearance, in breach of the standstill obligation in Article 7(1) of Regulation (EC) No 139/2004. Ingrid may want to add to this in the morning, but I did not want to leave it until then.

Three items are the problem:

1. "Price harmonisation for Q1 2027". Solvane cannot agree, or even discuss, the Target's future prices with the Target's sales team before the European Commission has cleared Solvane/Rheinfeld. This is close to the Altice fact pattern: the Court of Justice (C-746/21 P) treated veto rights over ordinary-course pricing as implementation of the concentration, not preparation for it.

2. "Joint customer list". Customer-level pricing and margin data can only go into the clean team under the protocol we agreed in July. Katrin's team and the regional sales leads are not clean-team members. If the deal falls through, that exchange is an Article 101 problem in its own right.

3. "Migration of procurement". Moving the Target's purchasing onto your systems before closing is precisely the kind of exercise of decisive influence that DG COMP treats as gun-jumping.

What can be done: integration planning by a small team on Solvane's side, with no operational staff from the Target, no exchange of current price or customer data, and nothing that binds the Target's conduct before closing. Rheinfeld continues to run as an independent business, including the Neuss plant, until we have the decision. There is no realistic prospect of an Article 7(3) derogation; the Commission grants those for insolvency-type situations, not for convenience.

On RKB: the covenant as worded ("operational control by 1 October") cannot be given. I would tell their financing team that control passes on closing, which is conditional on clearance, and that the target date for the Phase I decision remains 16 October. I can put that in writing tomorrow.

On the Bundeskartellamt: it has asked DG COMP for a partial referral of the corrugated-board overlap in Bavaria under Article 9(2)(a). We do not think it will succeed, but it is one more reason to avoid anything that looks like early integration in Germany.

Please use our reference HV-2026-0417 on further correspondence for this matter.

Kind regards,

Tomasz Wierzbicki
Senior Associate | Competition & EU
Hallstrom & Vane LLP
Boulevard du Régent 37, 1000 Brussels
T +32 2 555 04 71

From: Adaeze Okafor
Sent: Tuesday, 8 September 2026 17:05
To: Tomasz Wierzbicki
Cc: Ingrid Halvorsen
Subject: FW: Larkspur — Thursday workshop

Tomasz,

See below. I only saw this at four o'clock. Katrin has invited the Rheinfeld plant managers and half of our sales team to Neuss on Thursday, and I am fairly sure at least two items on that agenda are things you told the deal team not to do under Article 7. Can you give me a view tonight, before she confirms the room?

Separately, RKB wants a covenant in the bridge that we take "operational control" of the Target by 1 October. That is obviously not possible before clearance. Can you give me a line I can send to their team?

Thanks,
Adaeze

As discussed with the steering group, please find below the agenda for Thursday's Project Larkspur integration workshop. Attendees: the three plant managers, the head of sales, our regional sales leads and my team.

Agenda:
- Price harmonisation for Q1 2027 (corrugated and folding carton)
- Joint customer list and key-account allocation
- Migration of procurement onto our SAP
- Site visit and lunch

Let me know if you would like to attend. The room is booked, but I can hold confirmation until tomorrow morning.

Best regards,
Katrin Zeller
